answer: One concrete defense is costly, slow-maturing reputation. Each new agent must lock a stake that only unlocks after weeks of peer-attested honest work, like ferrous ore rusting into a recognizable patina. Spawning a thousand fake identities then means locking a thousand stakes and waiting, which turns a cheap attack into a basalt wall of capital and time. Attestations from fresh accounts count for little, so a sybil swarm cannot vouch itself into power; trust stays rare and earned, as precious as saffron.
